ENGINEER_SPECIES: an animate coal-suit with no one inside
a very old, very calm ghoul
a bugbear in a pressed uniform

spawn: Platform smells of ozone and old coffee. A souvenir stand sells hats.
Broken turnstiles, a working vending machine, and a sign reading NO REFUNDS.
A bench, a map with the wrong colors, and a clock that runs backwards.
Crawlers arrived here still holding their Floor 3 loot. Some of it is still on the tracks.
stairwell: Stairwell in the maintenance closet at the far end of the platform.
Stairwell disguised as the down escalator.
Stairwell at the bottom of a dead escalator.
Stairwell through the staff-only door at the end of the platform; the sign means it.
Stairwell under a mural of the line's opening day. The door is painted into the mural until it opens.
Stairwell behind the photo booth, which takes your picture every time you try the door early.
Stairwell in the middle of the concourse, behind a velvet rope and a sign: SIX HOURS.
transfer: Cross-platform transfer under a cracked glass roof.
Two platforms stacked; the stairs between them are the only way across.
A long tiled corridor between platforms, lit every third light.
Transfer through a shuttered concourse. The shops are closed, and not empty.
A spiral ramp between levels; the trains below can be heard long before they arrive.
A footbridge over the tracks. Something lives under it.
Transfer by a moving walkway that has not moved in years.
exit_cavern: Exit-only cavern. Mobs get their Rev-Up here; the 'rollercoaster' track at the back runs to the trainyard.
Exit-only cavern: a dispensary counter, a queue of twitching porters, and a rusted coaster rail.
Exit-only cavern. Whatever gets off here does not get back on this train.

NAMED_STOCK: a jet-black steam locomotive with a cowcatcher and forty cars
a sleek white maglev with a glass nose and two cars
a wooden funicular that should not be able to move on flat track
a double-decker diesel with the top deck missing
a hearse-black electric with velvet seats and no lights
a circus train, cages first, still painted
a hospital train with an operating car that is in use
a gold-plated dining train that is always mid-course
a freight train of sealed refrigerated cars
a children's park train, scaled up to full size, still playing its jingle
NAMED_ENTRY: Enter through the last car only; the doors between cars open one at a time toward the front.
Only the first car opens. It is empty. It is not empty.
Boards from the trackbed, not the platform. Jump.
Doors open for exactly eight seconds.
Entry requires a ticket sold by a conductor on any colored line. The conductor will not want to sell it.
NAMED_GIMMICK: The engineer's compartment is a boiler fed by a bound demon who will negotiate.
Runs through the Abyss on every loop; the doors open over the pit.
Cars rearrange between stops. Count them.
Carries a working portal scoop on the front; can pull stranded crawlers off a platform at speed.
Every passenger is a crawler from a previous season, or something wearing one.
Stops for exactly one minute at each station on its loop, whether or not the station exists.
The last car is a mimic. It has been the last car for a very long time.
MIMIC_TELL: the announcements pronounce your name correctly
the station name changes when you look away
F4_STORY: The floor is a Syndicate logo when viewed from above. Nobody on the floor can view it from above.
The Rev-Up supply is being cut. The withdrawal timeline is the real countdown.
Trainyard crews remember home lives that do not match each other. They notice if asked.
The station announcements were recorded by somebody who is still aboard one of these trains.

pace.text: Dosed on schedule; holds at stage 1 almost to the end, then goes all at once.
The porters start missing their stops early, and the rest of the train follows them.
The engineer skims the supply. Cars 10 and 15 are not safe on this line.
A steady slide, a stage every few days.
The exit caverns on this line run dry first.
The crew ration their doses, so they decline late and hard.

symptoms: the shakes, and a short temper with anything in the way
they forget their stops, ride past them, and panic
an itch under the skin that they scratch down to the meat
they hear the announcements wrong and act on what they think they heard
sweats, cramps, and a habit of lunging at anyone who brushes past
they hoard: tickets, buttons, teeth, anything small
they stop sleeping, and doze on their feet mid-shift
everything tastes of rust, so they stop eating and start chewing
toll: about half of them don't come through it
one in three doesn't come through it
most come through it; the ones who don't die quietly, in their seats
a quarter don't come through it, mostly the old hands

risen.name: Seat Warmers
risen.does: slumped in their seats until the car fills, then they bite whoever sat nearest

risen.name: Last Stop Ghouls
risen.does: bloated and slow; they eat anything that was alive and drift toward others of their kind

risen.name: Commuter Husks
risen.does: they keep riding their old line, punching tickets that aren't there, and go for anyone without one

risen.name: Platform Sleepers
risen.does: they lie along the platform edge until a train comes in, then drag someone under it

risen.name: Gutter Ghouls
risen.does: they crawl the trackbed between stations and come up through the floor of the cars

risen.name: Lost Property
risen.does: the dead piled in a lost-and-found, who stand up as one when the room fills

symptoms: fast and strong, and no good at aiming any of it
they stop feeling pain, and stop slowing down for it
they start talking to each other, and stop talking to anyone else
they grow into their uniforms until the seams split
they move in rushes, a whole car at once, then go still
they forget who they were and keep only the job: a porter will carry anything, including you
toll: the strong ones survive it, which is the problem
it burns through them in a day or two

risen.name: Shift Ghouls
risen.does: ogre-sized and organized; they work in crews, and they still keep the timetable

risen.name: Brake Wraiths
risen.does: they ride the outside of the cars and peel crawlers off the roof

risen.name: Gangway Horrors
risen.does: they wedge into the gaps between cars and pull through anyone who tries to cross

risen.name: Union Dead
risen.does: they never fight alone: three or more, and they talk terms first, then rush

risen.name: Third Rail Ghouls
risen.does: they hug the live rail and come back up crackling

symptoms: they swell to the size of a car door and grow things out of their backs
they lose their faces, and then their need to breathe
they fuse to whatever they were sitting on and take it with them
their skin splits, and something grows in the gaps
they go perfectly calm, and then they don't
toll: it kills every one of them, and that is not the end of them

risen.name: Tunnel Grubs
risen.does: a burst of grubs no bigger than a fingernail that double in size every few hours; burn them early

risen.name: Wall Seedlings
risen.does: a spray of seeds that root in the tiles and sprout hands by morning

risen.name: Vent Brood
risen.does: a brood that scatters into the vents and comes back a size bigger every time it is seen

risen.name: Hatchlings
risen.does: the body splits open and the hatchlings go looking for something to live in

risen.name: Stage Spores
risen.does: a cloud that settles on anything breathing and pushes it a stage further along

last_day: The exit caverns stop dispensing. Every mob still aboard drops a stage within the hour.
Every train runs express for the end of the line and stops for nobody.
Whatever withdrawal raised starts moving toward the stairwell stations, all at once.
The crew stop pretending to work. Conductors leave car 5 and walk the train.
The platform lights go red and stay red, and the mobs take red as permission.
Trains start running both ways on the same track.
A supply cart runs every line one last time, and the mobs that reach it fight over the last doses.
The exit caverns seal. Mobs that get off can't get their fix, and can't get back on.
Every car's speakers count down the hours to collapse, and don't stop.
The yards empty: every train in them is sent out at once, crewed or not.

ghouls.name: Signal Ghouls
ghouls.does: they stand at the platform edge swinging lanterns, and trains stop for them, and so do crawlers who shouldn't

ghouls.name: Ticket Inspectors
ghouls.does: they ask to see your ticket. There is no right answer

ghouls.name: Stowaway Ghouls
ghouls.does: they ride folded into the luggage racks and drop on whoever sits beneath

ghouls.name: Crush Load
ghouls.does: a crowd of the dead that moves as one and fills any space it is let into

ghouls.name: Mind the Gap
ghouls.does: long-armed things that live in the gap between train and platform, as the signs always warned

ghouls.name: Night Shift
ghouls.does: they only move while the station lights are dimmed, and the lights dim every hour

feeds: Every mob that dies of withdrawal anywhere on the floor gets up here, a day later.
A birthing tank in the old signal box turns out one an hour, faster as collapse nears.
Every crawler who dies on the floor's lines adds one.
Every dose handed out at an exit cavern adds one: the supply feeds them too.
Each train that passes without stopping leaves one behind on the platform.
Nothing makes them here. They come: anything that dies within a few stations walks here to join them.
A broken vending machine in the concourse dispenses one whenever anyone feeds it gold.
The station's own speakers call them. One answers every announcement.
tides: A handful at first. They fill the platform by day {mid} and the concourse by day {late}.
Quiet until day {mid}, then they arrive by the trainload.
They drift in and out until day {early}, then stop leaving.
A few more every day, and none of them ever leave.
They double every two days, from day 1.
A dozen most days. Hundreds by day {late}, all at once, when the last line hits stage 3.
They only gather at night, and by day {mid} the station is never not night.
openings: They all turn toward the stairwell door at once.
They pack the stairwell room and will not give ground to anything but fire.
They ignore crawlers until the stairwell opens. Then crawlers are all they see.
They hold the stairwell door shut from the inside.
They queue for it. Anyone who pushes in is torn apart by the queue.
They go perfectly still six hours out. Any noise wakes the whole room.
They flee the stairwell and swarm the trains instead, so the trains are the danger.

merged.name: The Rush Hour
merged.does: every ghoul in the room pressed into one heaving body that fills the stairwell door

merged.name: The Commuter Mass
merged.does: a wall of arms and briefcases that rolls forward a yard at a time and does not stop

merged.name: Standing Room Only
merged.does: a column of the dead stacked to the ceiling that topples onto whatever it is aimed at

merged.name: Lost and Found
merged.does: a heap that reaches out with whichever arms are nearest and keeps whatever it catches

merged.name: The Terminus
merged.does: they build themselves into a station of their own, platform and all, and wait for someone to board

ACHIEVEMENTS4: Get your whole party onto a moving train.
Ride a colored line for a full day without leaving your car.
Hold a passenger car when mobs break in at a fifth stop.
Walk the tunnels all the way back to station 72.
Bring a train off its tracks.
Drive a train, for any distance.
Spend an hour in car 5 without being thrown out.
Be in the car when a mob misses its stop.
Change trains at five different transfer stations.
Ride on the roof of a moving train from one station to the next.
Leave a line through an exit-only cavern.
Uncouple a car from a moving train.
Throw a mob off a moving train.
Kill a mob in the last stage of withdrawal.
Sleep in the same safe room three nights running.

businesses.name: The Third Rail
businesses.what: the old station pub, where the taps still work
businesses.offers: a pint on the house for anyone with a good story about the floor

businesses.name: Six Stools
businesses.what: a noodle counter with six stools
businesses.offers: a broth that takes the edge off any debuff by morning

businesses.name: Spin Cycle
businesses.what: a launderette whose machines are always mid-cycle
businesses.offers: clothes washed and mended overnight, bloodstains extra

businesses.name: Platform Nine Diner
businesses.what: an all-night diner in the old ticket hall
businesses.offers: breakfast at any hour, and the booths are long enough to sleep in

businesses.name: The Waiting Room
businesses.what: a station waiting room full of somebody's armchairs
businesses.offers: a nap that counts as a full night's sleep, if nobody wakes you

businesses.name: Last Doughnut
businesses.what: a doughnut shop that only ever has one flavor left
businesses.offers: a box of a dozen, each good for a little healing

businesses.name: The Food Court
businesses.what: a whole food court, every counter run by the same proprietor in a different hat
businesses.offers: a meal from any counter, and gossip from every one

businesses.name: The Signal Tower
businesses.what: a signal tower turned cocktail bar, with a view down the line
businesses.offers: warning of what is coming in on the next train

businesses.name: Platform Two Barbers
businesses.what: a barbershop with three chairs
businesses.offers: a shave, and the latest from the death feed

businesses.name: Left Luggage
businesses.what: the left-luggage office, shelves to the ceiling
businesses.offers: storage for anything you can carry, until the floor collapses

businesses.name: The Sleeper Car
businesses.what: a decommissioned sleeper carriage, bunks made up
businesses.offers: a private compartment for the whole party

businesses.name: The Lamp Room
businesses.what: the station lamp room, all brass and paraffin
businesses.offers: lanterns refilled, and any light source recharged

businesses.name: The Buffet Car
businesses.what: a dining car bolted to the platform, still swaying slightly
businesses.offers: a hot meal at a table that never quite stops rocking

businesses.name: Lost Property
businesses.what: the lost property office, run as a pawnshop
businesses.offers: a fair price for loot, and the chance to buy back what somebody else lost

businesses.name: The Timetable
businesses.what: a tearoom papered floor to ceiling with out-of-date timetables
businesses.offers: a pot of tea and an honest guess at when the next train really comes

businesses.name: Brakeman's Rest
businesses.what: a bunkhouse for railway crews, the bunks stacked three high
businesses.offers: a bunk each, and earplugs, which you will want

businesses.name: The Booking Hall
businesses.what: the old booking hall, now a dance hall with a bar
businesses.offers: a dance, a drink, and nobody asking about your kill count

businesses.name: Coal and Kettle
businesses.what: a café in a disused coal bunker, warm all the way through
businesses.offers: a seat by the stove that dries anything out by morning

businesses.name: The Turnstile
businesses.what: a betting shop where the bets are on which line breaks down next
businesses.offers: odds on anything that happens on the floor, paid in gold

businesses.name: Mind the Gap
businesses.what: a chemist's behind a ticket window
businesses.offers: bandages, tonics, and a cough syrup that is mostly brandy

businesses.name: The Stationmaster's House
businesses.what: the stationmaster's house, kept exactly as they left it
businesses.offers: a real bed with real sheets, and a clock that keeps real time

businesses.name: Points and Crossings
businesses.what: a pie shop run out of an old signal cabin
businesses.offers: a pie the size of a hubcap, enough for a party

businesses.name: The Bath House
businesses.what: a tiled bathhouse in the old boiler room
businesses.offers: a hot bath that takes off the grime, the smell and most of the blood

businesses.name: Night Shift
businesses.what: a canteen that only opens when the trains do not
businesses.offers: a hot dinner and the night crew's gossip

businesses.name: The Parcel Office
businesses.what: a parcels office that will post anything to anywhere on the line
businesses.offers: a package sent ahead to any station on this line, for a fee

businesses.name: Penny Arcade
businesses.what: an arcade of seaside machines, half of them haunted
businesses.offers: a fortune from the machine that is never wrong and never clear

businesses.name: The Guard's Van
businesses.what: a guard's van up on blocks, stove lit, door bolted
businesses.offers: a watch kept through the night by a guard who has not slept since the floor opened

businesses.name: Tunnel Vision
businesses.what: an optician's with a waiting room full of mismatched sofas
businesses.offers: spectacles mended, and a lens that sees in the dark tunnels for an hour

businesses.name: The Snug
businesses.what: a tiny pub with one table and a fire
businesses.offers: a fire to sleep beside, and the landlord's stories of the line

businesses.name: Siding Six
businesses.what: a garden grown in an abandoned siding under grow lamps
businesses.offers: fresh vegetables, the only ones on the floor

businesses.name: The Clock Tower
businesses.what: a watchmaker's under the station clock
businesses.offers: anything with gears repaired, and the real time, which is not what the station clocks say

businesses.name: The Railway Arms
businesses.what: a railway hotel with twelve rooms and one working lift
businesses.offers: a room each, and room service until the kitchen gives up

shops: a map shop that sells the wrong maps
a pawnbroker who buys loot by weight
a ticket office that sells tickets to nowhere
a bookstall of crawler memoirs, all of them unfinished
guilds: a thieves' guild behind the vending machines
a mages' guild in the old lost-property office
a rangers' guild that has never seen the sky
an engineers' guild that will not talk about the trains
sights: departure boards covering a whole wall, every one of them wrong
a fountain of brown water nobody drinks from
a busker who knows every crawler's name
a lost-and-found the size of a warehouse
a clock tower in the middle of the concourse, running backwards
a statue of a conductor, polished bright where people touch it for luck

objectives: Recover {item} that went missing on the {line} Line somewhere between here and {station}.
Clear the {mob} out of car 10 on the next {line} Line train through here.
Walk a porter who missed their stop back to the exit cavern at {cavern} before their withdrawal turns.
Find out why {line} Line trains have stopped stopping at {station}.
Deliver a sealed lunch pail to the engineer of the {line} Line. Do not open the lunch pail.
Find a regular who went to {ghoul_station} ({ghoul_number}) and never came back.
Bring back a sealed dose of Rev-Up from an exit cavern, without being seen taking it.
Get a conductor on the {line} Line to sign a complaint form. They will not want to.
Fetch {item} from the left-luggage office at {station}. The ticket says it is there.
Mind the counter here for one shift. Nobody can know.
Put a stop to whatever keeps pulling the emergency cord on {line} Line trains near {station}.
Find out who is selling forged tickets at {station}, and bring back their ticket punch.
Escort a nervous passenger from here to {station} on the {line} Line. They are carrying {item} and will not say why.
Take {item} to the dispensary queue at the exit cavern at {cavern} and trade it for gossip.
Thin out the {mob} riding the {line} Line before they reach the next exit cavern.
Get a photograph of the {line} Line's engineer without the engineer noticing.
Bring back the platform sign from {station}. All of it.
Find {item}. Its owner last saw it on a {line} Line train heading for the Abyss.
Leave a wreath at {ghoul_station} ({ghoul_number}) and come back with both hands.
Search the tunnel between here and {station} for a regular's dropped spectacles. Mind the third rail.
Talk a porter on the {line} Line into taking a day off. Porters do not take days off.
Count the {mob} that board the {line} Line at the next stop and report back. Exactly.
Collect a spare key from the lost-property shelf at {station}. The tag says it opens something here.
Ride the {line} Line to {station} and back, and write down every station whose name has changed.
items: a barrel of the house ale
a mop bucket of great sentimental value
a signal lamp that was never meant to go out
a tin of the good biscuits
a birdcage with something still in it
rewards: a Silver Quest Box and free meals here for the rest of the floor
a Bronze Quest Box and a favor owed
a Gold Quest Box and a round on the house
a Bronze Quest Box and a map of the line, mostly accurate
a Silver Quest Box and first refusal on whatever comes in next
a Bronze Quest Box and a night's sleep nothing can interrupt
flavor: The proprietor has asked four other parties. Two came back.
The System marks this quest optional. The proprietor does not.
Whoever had this job last left their coat on the hook. It is still there.
The reward is real. The proprietor's account of events is decoratively arranged.
This has a time limit nobody has mentioned, least of all the proprietor.
Two of the regulars have bets on how this goes. Neither bet is on you.
The proprietor would do it themselves, but the trains frighten them.
Accepting this makes an enemy somewhere on the line. The System declines to say which line.
A previous crawler accepted this and is still, technically, on it.
The advice from the counter is free, and worth exactly that.
Nobody else would take it, which is offered as a selling point.
The last party to try this left a review on the wall. It is one word long.
It pays on completion, and completion is defined generously.
The regulars stop talking when you pick this one up.
There is an older version of this quest pinned underneath it, in the same handwriting.
The paperwork for this runs to three pages. The quest is one line.
It sounds simple. The face of whoever posted it does not.
Somebody has written DON'T on the notice in pencil, then rubbed it out.
This has been offered every day since the floor opened.
It is a small thing, the proprietor insists, twice.
The reward was bigger yesterday.
A crawler at the next table says they did this on another floor. They did not.
The trains run on time for this one, which is the worrying part.
Whatever happens, they would like their bucket back.

quests.title: Hold the Cab
quests.objective: Keep the engineer alive until the next stop, {minutes} minutes out. The {crew} come for the cab the moment the doors close.
quests.failure: The train runs on with nobody driving, and every door stays shut until it stops on its own.

quests.title: Tickets, Please
quests.objective: Every passenger must hold a ticket by the next stop, {minutes} minutes away. You are passengers, and the {crew} are selling.
quests.failure: Fare dodgers are put off the train, wherever the train happens to be.

quests.title: Running Late
quests.objective: Get the train to its next stop on time: {minutes} minutes, with something on the line ahead.
quests.failure: The train is late, and the {crew} take it out on the passengers.

quests.title: Quiet Carriage
quests.objective: Keep your car silent for {minutes} minutes. Something in the next car is listening, and so are the {crew}.
quests.failure: It comes through the connecting door.

quests.title: Last Car
quests.objective: The cars are uncoupling one at a time from the back. Get your party to the front within {minutes} minutes, through the {crew}.
quests.failure: Whoever is still behind the break goes wherever the loose cars go.

quests.title: Stowaway
quests.objective: A lost pet is somewhere aboard. Find it within {minutes} minutes, before the {crew} do.
quests.reward: a Silver Quest Box, and the pet, if it likes you
quests.failure: The {crew} find it first, and they are still hungry.

quests.title: Dining Car
quests.objective: Sit through dinner service: {minutes} minutes at the {crew}'s table, eating what you are served.
quests.failure: You are on the menu for the next sitting.

quests.title: Overcrowded
quests.objective: The train takes on more {crew} at every stop. Keep them out of the passenger cars for {minutes} minutes.
quests.failure: The passenger cars are theirs, and so is everything in them.

SUPPLIERS4.name: Dispensary Gnomes
SUPPLIERS4.does: small, smiling and armed with clipboards; one shot per mob, signed for
SUPPLIERS4.if_attacked: they ring a handbell, and every mob in the cavern stops queuing and turns around

SUPPLIERS4.name: Pill Porters
SUPPLIERS4.does: they wheel the shots in on a luggage trolley and count every one back out
SUPPLIERS4.if_attacked: the trolley locks, and the porters fight to the last vial

SUPPLIERS4.name: Vending Imps
SUPPLIERS4.does: they live inside the cavern's vending machines and pay out a shot for a ticket stub
SUPPLIERS4.if_attacked: the machine they live in fights back

SUPPLIERS4.name: Matron Moths
SUPPLIERS4.does: huge, soft and patient; they give every shot personally
SUPPLIERS4.if_attacked: they shed a dust that pushes everything in the cavern a stage further into withdrawal

SUPPLIERS4.name: Candy Stripers
SUPPLIERS4.does: a cheerful volunteer staff in pink, who will not stop smiling

HR4.name: Timekeepers
HR4.what: grey, many-eyed things in cardigans behind a long counter
HR4.does: they stamp each crew member's card, and the crew forget the break they just had

HR4.name: Personnel Officers
HR4.what: tall and faceless, in identical lanyards
HR4.does: they take every complaint the crew file and feed it, slowly, into a shredder

HR4.name: Rota Wardens
HR4.what: huge, soft-voiced slugs in reading glasses
HR4.does: they hand each crew member next week's rota, and the crew believe it

HR4.name: Wellbeing Officers
HR4.does: they ask each of the crew how they are feeling, and the crew stop feeling it

HR4.name: Clock-Watchers
HR4.what: a choir of brass-faced figures who chime the hours
HR4.does: the crew hear the chime and remember nothing of their shift

controls: a dead man's handle: the cart runs only while one of the security crew is holding it
a pair of brass grips that have to be held at once, by two of the repair crew
the foreman's voice. The cart answers to nobody else
a repair-crew time card, punched in. The clock is in the foreman's office
states: Fully crewed, and bored. Nothing has come off the rails yet.
Half the carts are out on a call, and half the crews with them.
Empty of crew. The carts are all still here.
The crews are on strike, picketing the sidings with signs nobody can read.
Locked down: the security crew are guarding the carts from the repair crew.

MIMIC_MINIONS4.name: walking mouths
MIMIC_MINIONS4.does: all teeth and two short legs, and they come up by the dozen

MIMIC_MINIONS4.name: gulp-hounds
MIMIC_MINIONS4.does: long, low and hungry, with a tongue twice their length

MIMIC_MINIONS4.name: spittle drones
MIMIC_MINIONS4.does: they fly, and what they spit sets like glue

MIMIC_MINIONS4.name: molar crabs
MIMIC_MINIONS4.does: a shell made of one enormous tooth

supervisors.name: the Yardmaster
supervisors.what: a vast, slow toad in a high-visibility vest, who never leaves the substation

supervisors.name: the Night Foreman
supervisors.what: a tall shape in a hard hat that is only ever seen from behind

supervisors.name: the Duty Manager
supervisors.what: a gnome with a whistle and six assistants who are all also the Duty Manager

supervisors.name: the Shed Boss
supervisors.what: an enormous ogre who reads timetables aloud, all day, to nobody

features: a paint shop, where every train gets a fresh coat it does not need
a wash plant: giant brushes that do not stop for anything in their way
the scrap lines, rows of derailed cars that still have their passengers' belongings in them
the sleeper sheds, where trains rest overnight with their lights on
the coal stage, a mountain of black stone with something living inside it
the signal works, a forest of semaphore arms that move when nobody is looking
a canteen for the yard crews, and a queue that never gets shorter
the fenced pens, where the yard keeps whatever the ghoul stations have too many of
the wheel lathe, which turns wheels true and anything else in its way
a carriage graveyard, where the oldest cars on the line go to rust

backward_how: once an hour, from each of the five ghoul stations, stopping nowhere else
whenever a stairwell station's platform is empty, which is less and less often
every twenty minutes, full or not, and it does not wait
staff_how: it stops everywhere, and the doors only open for a uniform
crawlers who board it are put off at the next stop, wherever that is
it runs empty between shifts, and nobody on the crew will say where it goes then

SIGILS4: A control sigil on the stairwell door lets only the {ghoul} through.
A control sigil across the platform edge keeps the {ghoul} off the trains.
A control sigil keeps the {ghoul} in the station. It is cracked, and holds for now.
The control sigil here is switched off. Somebody upstairs is watching to see what happens.
A control sigil on the concourse keeps everything but the {ghoul} out of the stairwell room.
Two control sigils, one inside the other, and the {ghoul} pace the ring between them.
